description:
A guard helper clause whose body is one call to a function that only aborts makes the guard false. The reifier already treats it so (GuardCallee::always_fails, src/dispatch_matrix/pattern.rs). The walk that collects what a dispatch needs (collect_requirements, src/compiler2/jobs/dispatch.rs) still descends into the aborting call's arguments and requires each call there as a guard helper. With raise a macro, tuple_size/1's raising clause calls exception/1, and the guard is refused as not dispatch-pure.

Change: when a clause body is one call whose callee only aborts (an extern declared to return never, or a helper whose every clause body is such a call), the dispatch requires only that callee. An extern's never is read from its declaration, not from a settled wire.

Proof: fixture with def f(x) when tuple_size(x) == 2 over a non-tuple, Elixir oracle, three paths; a drive test that the dispatch records no requirement for the arguments of the aborting call. Spiked on a59d95d01: the whole suite shows no guard refusal with fz-3sy.8 applied.
title: A dispatch asks only for the aborting call when a guard helper clause is one call that never returns
